name: Plan
tagline: Before writing a single line of code, teams must align on product vision, user needs, and architectural boundaries.
summary: You have mastered the foundational Plan stage of the DevOps lifecycle—from structuring Epics and User Stories in Product Backlogs to defining Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and Error Budgets for production resilience.
heroSnippet:
# Jira & Azure Boards · Sprint Backlog & Acceptance Criteria
epic: "EPIC-404: Global Zero-Downtime DevOps Automation"
sprint: "Sprint 24 · Goal: Establish Business Value Roadmaps"
tooling_ecosystem: ["Jira Software", "Trello Kanban", "Azure Boards", "Confluence PRDs"]

curriculum.title: Requirements Gathering & User Needs Analysis
curriculum.description: Learn how to translate vague business goals and customer feedback into concrete, technical requirements and actionable product features without ambiguity.
objectives: Conduct stakeholder interviews and user research workshops
Distinguish between functional and non-functional requirements (NFRs)
Document clear scope boundaries to prevent scope creep during sprints

curriculum.title: Epics, User Stories & Acceptance Criteria (INVEST)
curriculum.description: Master the art of breaking down large Epics into bite-sized User Stories adhering to the INVEST criteria, complete with testable Acceptance Criteria using Given-When-Then.
objectives: Write user stories focused on customer value ("As a user, I want... so that...")
Apply the INVEST criteria (Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable)
Formulate unambiguous Behavior-Driven Acceptance Criteria (BDD)

curriculum.title: Product Backlog Refinement & Sprint Planning
curriculum.description: Organize and prioritize product backlogs using value vs risk frameworks, conduct story point estimation with Planning Poker, and execute high-velocity Sprint Planning sessions.
objectives: Prioritize backlog items using MoSCoW and Weighted Shortest Job First (WSJF)
Estimate technical effort using Fibonacci story points and Planning Poker
Establish sprint goals and calculate realistic team capacity and velocity

curriculum.title: Definition of Ready (DoR) & Definition of Done (DoD)
curriculum.description: Establish quality gates that govern when a task can enter a sprint (DoR) and when code is truly ready for customer release (DoD), eliminating technical debt.
objectives: Define mandatory DoR checkpoints before developers begin coding
Construct comprehensive DoD checklists including unit tests, code review, and CI build pass
Align cross-functional QA, DevOps, and Dev teams on shared completion standards

curriculum.title: SRE Reliability Engineering: SLOs, SLIs & Error Budgets
curriculum.description: Bridge software engineering and operational resilience by defining quantitative Service Level Indicators (SLIs), realistic Service Level Objectives (SLOs), and Error Budgets.
objectives: Select meaningful SLIs (latency, availability, error rate, throughput)
Calculate mathematically sound SLO targets (e.g., 99.9% vs 99.99%)
Use Error Budget burn rates to dynamically balance feature velocity against reliability work

curriculum.title: STRIDE Threat Modeling & DevSecOps Architecture
curriculum.description: Shift security left into the Plan phase by identifying potential security vulnerabilities during architectural design using Microsoft STRIDE threat modeling framework.
objectives: Analyze system diagrams for Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, and Elevation of Privilege
Write Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) to document security tradeoffs
Embed security verification tasks directly into sprint backlogs

learningPath.title: Conduct User Needs Discovery & Define Product Scope
learningPath.description: Meet with stakeholders to map out customer journeys, identify core pain points, and define functional boundary limits.
learningPath.keyTakeaway: Always ground technical tasks in tangible end-user value.

learningPath.title: Construct the Product Backlog with INVEST User Stories
learningPath.description: Write atomic user stories with clear acceptance criteria. Group related stories under strategic Epics within Jira or Azure Boards.
learningPath.keyTakeaway: A story must be testable—if you cannot verify it with Given-When-Then, it is not ready.

learningPath.title: Establish Team Velocity, DoR & DoD Quality Gates
learningPath.description: Run Planning Poker to assign story points. Formulate strict Definition of Ready and Definition of Done contracts across developers and QA.
learningPath.keyTakeaway: DoD prevents unfinished code from masquerading as complete features.

learningPath.title: Define Production SLO Targets and Error Budgets
learningPath.description: Define exact availability and latency thresholds for core user journeys. Establish error budget policies for freezing new features when stability drops.
learningPath.keyTakeaway: 100% availability is impossible and prohibitively expensive; aim for what keeps users happy.

learningPath.title: Perform STRIDE Threat Modeling & Finalize Roadmap
learningPath.description: Review architecture diagrams for security risks before writing code. Lock in the sprint backlog and launch Sprint 01.
learningPath.keyTakeaway: Fixing a security flaw in the planning phase costs 100x less than fixing it after production breach.

quiz.question: What is the primary difference between an Epic and a User Story in Agile DevOps planning?
options: An Epic is written by developers, while User Stories are written by customers
An Epic is a large strategic body of work spanning multiple sprints, which is broken down into smaller, bite-sized User Stories
An Epic represents technical bugs, whereas User Stories represent new features
There is no difference; they are exact synonyms in Scrum
quiz.explanation: Epics represent major business initiatives or large features that require several sprints to complete. During backlog grooming, teams decompose Epics into individual User Stories that can be designed, coded, and tested within a single sprint.

quiz.question: Which of the following describes the "T" in the INVEST criteria for high-quality User Stories?
options: Time-bound: Must take exactly 8 hours to complete
Technical: Must contain database schema definitions
Testable: Must have clear acceptance criteria so QA or automated tests can verify its completion
Traceable: Must be linked to a specific git commit ID before coding begins
quiz.explanation: Testable means the user story provides unambiguous criteria (usually Behavior-Driven Given-When-Then format) so the team can verify whether the code meets the exact requirements.

quiz.question: In Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), what happens when a team exhausts its "Error Budget" for the month?
options: The team receives a financial bonus for deploying high amounts of code
Feature releases are temporarily halted or slowed down to focus 100% engineering effort on bug fixes, reliability, and technical debt
The production servers are automatically shut down until next month
The DevOps lead deletes the CI/CD pipeline
quiz.explanation: An Error Budget is `100% - SLO`. For example, if the SLO is 99.9%, the Error Budget is 0.1% of downtime/errors. When exhausted, the governance policy dictates shifting focus entirely to reliability improvements until the system stabilizes.

handsOnLabs.title: Agile Backlog Setup & INVEST Story Crafting Lab
handsOnLabs.prerequisites: No prerequisite coding skills required; familiarity with web browsers.
handsOnLabs.desc: Create a production-ready Product Backlog structure from scratch. You will take a high-level e-commerce requirement, formulate 3 INVEST-compliant user stories, and construct unambiguous Given-When-Then acceptance criteria.
objectives: Initialize a clean Scrum sprint structure with Epics and Stories
Decompose "User Checkout" into 3 independent, testable user stories
Draft Definition of Ready (DoR) and Definition of Done (DoD) agreements
Assign Fibonacci story points based on technical complexity
handsOnLabs.codeSnippet:
### User Story: EP-104 - Secure Cart Checkout
**As a** registered customer,
**I want to** select my saved credit card and complete checkout with one click,
**So that I** can purchase items quickly without re-typing shipping details every time.

#### Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then):
- **Scenario 1: Successful One-Click Checkout**
  - **Given** the user is logged in with a valid saved Visa card ending in 4242
  - **When** the user clicks "Pay & Place Order" inside the shopping cart
  - **Then** the system authorizes the payment within 2 seconds
  - **And** generates an order confirmation number and sends an email invoice.

- **Scenario 2: Expired Card Handling**
  - **Given** the user's default saved card has expired
  - **When** the user clicks "Pay & Place Order"
  - **Then** the system blocks submission and displays a red badge: "Card Expired. Please update payment method."

handsOnLabs.title: Production SLO & Error Budget Calculation Lab
handsOnLabs.prerequisites: Basic math/percentage calculations and understanding of HTTP error codes.
handsOnLabs.desc: Construct a quantitative SRE Service Level Objective configuration for a high-traffic microservice. Calculate exact monthly downtime thresholds and configure automated alert rules when error budgets burn too rapidly.
objectives: Formulate SLI equations for Availability and P99 Latency
Calculate exact monthly downtime allowance for a 99.95% availability target
Write Prometheus alert rules for Multi-Window Multi-Burn-Rate alerting
Establish governance runbooks for frozen sprint deployments upon budget exhaustion
handsOnLabs.codeSnippet:
apiVersion: sre.google.com/v1alpha1
kind: ServiceLevelObjective
metadata:
  name: payment-gateway-latency-slo
  namespace: production
spec:
  service: payment-gateway-svc
  target: 99.95 # 99.95% of requests must succeed fast
  timeWindow: 30d
  errorBudgetAllowanceMinutes: 21.6 # 30 days * 24h * 60m * 0.0005
  serviceLevelIndicator:
    requestLatency:
      threshold: 250ms # P99 latency must be under 250ms
      metricQuery: |
        sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="payment-gateway",le="0.25"}[5m]))
        /
        sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{service="payment-gateway"}[5m]))
  alertingPolicies:
    - burnRate: 14.4 # Burn 2% of budget in 1 hour
      severity: CRITICAL
      notificationChannel: "#sre-alerts-paging"
